transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A persistent funny smell after cleaning usually points to one of three things: hidden food residue in places you can't easily see (like the drip tray at the back or under the shelves), mould growing in the air vents or evaporator area, or less commonly, an electrical issue. First, please check if there is any burning smell or scorching marks near the plug or the back of the unit; if so, unplug it immediately and do not use it again. If it smells like rotting food or damp/musty, it’s likely a blockage in the defrost drain (which empties into a tray at the bottom rear) or mould in the vents. If it smells like burning plastic, it could be an electrical fault. Could you tell me:
1. Does the smell resemble rotting food/eggs, or does it smell like burning plastic/electrics?
2. Are the fridge and freezer compartments still getting cold as they should?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

It smells like hot plastic, an electrical sort of burning smell, not rotten food. It's stronger round the back of the fridge than inside it. The fridge and freezer are both still cold, and the plug feels a bit warm.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because the smell is of hot plastic/electrics and it is strongest at the back with a warm plug, this is an electrical safety fault. The appliance must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it. The most likely causes are:
1. A failing compressor start relay or overload protector inside (often near the plug/back) which can overheat and smell of burning plastic before failing completely.
2. An internal wiring insulation breakdown causing a short or earth leak as components heat up.
3. The mains lead or plug itself overheating due to poor contact or damage. Please unplug the fridge-freezer immediately from the wall socket. Do not try to reset any trips repeatedly, and do not attempt to open the back panel or test electrical parts yourself. Isolate it safely and arrange for a qualified engineer to diagnose and repair the fault.

candidates: Spoilt food residue in hidden areas (drain pan, drip tray, seals) (high)
Mould/mildew in the evaporator compartment or air ducts (medium)
